fields.title: Day 29 — Nothing Can Separate Us
fields.body_html:
“For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor principalities, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers, neither height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.”

— Romans 8:38–39 (BSB)

What’s the scariest thing you can imagine? Now here’s the good news: it can’t separate you from God’s love.

Paul wrote these words to Christians in Rome. Some of them would soon face terrible persecution for following Jesus. Paul himself had been beaten, shipwrecked, thrown in prison and chased from town to town. He knew about hard times. And he asked a question: “Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall trouble or distress or persecution or famine or nakedness or danger or sword?” (Romans 8:35).

Then he answered with one of the most powerful lists in the Bible. Look at all the things that cannot separate you from God’s love:

  • Death or life. Nothing in life, and not even death itself.
  • Angels or principalities. No spiritual power, not even the devil.
  • The present or the future. Nothing happening right now, and nothing that could ever happen.
  • Any powers. No person, government or force in the world.
  • Height or depth. Nothing up high or down low.
  • Anything else in all creation. In case Paul missed anything, this covers it!

Paul said he was “convinced.” He was absolutely sure.

Think about all the storms we’ve talked about this month: fear, worry, sadness, death, hard things at home, temptation, unfair treatment, weakness. Not one of them can separate you from God’s love. Not a bad grade. Not a mistake you made. Not a bully. Not a sickness. Not moving to a new place. Nothing.

A few verses earlier, Paul wrote, “in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us” (Romans 8:37). Not because we’re strong, but because of Him who loves us.

The storm might rage. The waves might crash. But the love of God that is in Christ Jesus is like an unbreakable rope that holds you tight. And it will never, ever let you go.

Think about it: What’s something you’ve worried might separate you from God’s love? What does this verse say about it?

Try this: Write Romans 8:38–39 on a card, and add your own “neither…nor…” to the list, like “neither a bad day nor my mistakes.” Keep it somewhere you’ll see it often.

Dear God, thank You that nothing in all creation can separate me from Your love. Not death, not life, not the present or the future, not anything. When storms come, help me remember that Your love holds me tight and will never let me go. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

fields.title: Day 30 — An Anchor for the Soul
fields.body_html:
“We have this hope as an anchor for the soul, firm and secure.”

— Hebrews 6:19 (BSB)

Have you ever seen a big ship’s anchor? It’s a heavy iron hook attached to the ship by a strong chain. When the sailors drop it, it sinks all the way to the bottom of the sea and digs into the ground.

Why do ships need anchors? Because without one, the wind and waves would push the ship all over the place. In a storm, a ship without an anchor could be smashed against the rocks. But a ship with a good anchor stays put. The waves still crash. The wind still blows. The ship still rocks up and down. But it doesn’t drift away.

The Bible says we have an “anchor for the soul.” What is it? Hope.

Not “hope” like “I hope it doesn’t rain tomorrow,” which just means wishing. Bible hope is much stronger than that. It means being certain about something that hasn’t happened yet, because God promised it.

And where is our anchor fixed? The verses around today’s verse tell us: in Jesus Himself, who has gone ahead of us into God’s presence. Our anchor isn’t dug into our own feelings, or into how well things are going. It’s dug into Jesus, who is alive, who never changes and who has promised never to leave us.

That’s why our hope is “firm and secure.” The storms can’t pull it loose, because it’s holding on to someone who can’t be moved.

Look back at this month. You’ve learned that storms come to everyone. You’ve learned what to do when you’re afraid and when you’re worried or sad. fields.title: Conclusion: Standing Strong
fields.body_html:
You did it! Thirty days of learning how to stand strong in the storms of life.

Think back over everything you’ve learned. You started with the wise builder who built his house on the rock, and you learned that storms come to everyone. What matters is the foundation.

You learned what to do when you’re afraid: put your trust in God, remember your Shepherd, be strong and courageous, and face your giants like David did. You learned to cast your worries on God, to pray instead of worry, and that it’s okay to be sad, because Jesus cried too. You learned that we grieve with hope, that God is a Father who never leaves, and that He works all things for good.

You learned how to face temptation: look for the way out, run like Joseph, refuse to be squeezed into the world’s mold, make up your mind like Daniel, resist the devil and get back up when you fall. You put on the armor of God. You saw three young men stand in the fire, and Daniel keep praying when it was dangerous, and Esther risk everything to do what was right.

And you learned that when life isn’t fair, when prayers don’t turn out the way you hoped, and when you feel tired and weak, God’s ways are higher, His grace is enough, and nothing can separate you from His love.

That’s a strong foundation!

If you haven’t trusted Jesus yet

The best foundation of all is Jesus Himself. If you haven’t trusted Him yet, you can today. He died on the cross to pay for your sins and rose again, and He offers you forgiveness and a hope that will never let you go. You can pray something like this:

Dear Jesus, I know I have sinned, and I need You. I believe You died for me and rose again. I trust You as my Savior, and I want to follow You as my Lord. Please be my Rock and my anchor. Thank You for loving me. Amen.

If you prayed that, tell a parent, a pastor or another Christian you trust, so they can celebrate with you and help you grow.

What’s next

A tree with strong roots and a sturdy trunk doesn’t just stand there. It spreads out its branches and gives shade to others.

In Book 5, you’ll learn how God’s love reaches out through you: loving your family, being a true friend, forgiving people who hurt you, being part of God’s family at church, and caring about people all over the world. You’ll learn that the greatest commandments are to love God and love your neighbor.

Until then, keep building on the Rock. Keep your anchor in Jesus. And remember: no storm is bigger than your God.

“But the Lord is faithful, and He will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one.”

— 2 Thessalonians 3:3 (BSB)
